* {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Saga Prefecture]] |draft}}{{Munakata Faith|draft}} [[simple:{{PAGENAME|draft}}]]

{{Short description|Shinto Shrine on an Island in Saga Prefecture}} {{Draft topics|biography|literature|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231202061217|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} {{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg |caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}} |draft}} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!|draft}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com|draft}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]],<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" /> whose poem was written by [[Yamanoue no Okura]], and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata
It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref>
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|Youminglu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

* {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Saga Prefecture]] |draft}}{{Munakata Faith|draft}} [[simple:{{PAGENAME|draft}}]]

{{Short description|Shinto Shrine on an Island in Saga Prefecture}} {{Draft topics|biography|literature|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231202061217|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} {{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg |caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}} |draft}} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!|draft}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com|draft}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]],<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" /> whose poem was written by [[Yamanoue no Okura]], and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata
It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref>
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

* {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Saga Prefecture]] |draft}}{{Munakata Faith|draft}} [[simple:{{PAGENAME|draft}}]]

{{Short description|Shinto Shrine on an Island in Saga Prefecture}} {{Draft topics|biography|literature|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231202061217|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} {{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg |caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}} |draft}} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!|draft}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com|draft}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />, and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata
It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref>
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

{{Short description|Shinto Shrine on an Island in Saga Prefecture}} {{Draft topics|biography|literature|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231202061217|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} {{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg |caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}} |draft}} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!|draft}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com|draft}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />. It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref> and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata [[File:Wajinden_diagram.svg|thumb|map illustrating the path from the [[Daifang Commandery|Daifeng commandery]] to [[Yamatai]], and its distances in the [[Wajinden]]. See Matsurokoku around the middle for the locatiton of the shrine]]
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

* {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Saga Prefecture]] |draft}}{{Munakata Faith|draft}} [[simple:{{PAGENAME|draft}}]]

{{Short description|Shinto Shrine on an Island in Saga Prefecture}} {{Draft topics|biography|literature|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231202061217|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} {{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg | caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|33|21|N|129|53|26|E}} | location = Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}}|draft }} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!|draft}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com|draft}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />. It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref> and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata [[File:Wajinden_diagram.svg|thumb|map illustrating the path from the [[Daifang Commandery|Daifeng commandery]] to [[Yamatai]], and its distances in the [[Wajinden]]. See Matsurokoku around the middle for the locatiton of the shrine]]
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

----
{{Short description|Shinto Shrine on an Island in Saga Prefecture}} {{Draft topics|biography|literature|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}}
{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg | caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|33|21|N|129|53|26|E}} | location = Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}}|draft }} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!|draft}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com|draft}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />. It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref> and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata [[File:Wajinden_diagram.svg|thumb|map illustrating the path from the [[Daifang Commandery|Daifeng commandery]] to [[Yamatai]], and its distances in the [[Wajinden]]. See Matsurokoku around the middle for the locatiton of the shrine]]
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg | caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|33|21|N|129|53|26|E}} | location = Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}}|draft }} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-14 |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514023648/https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />. It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref> and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata [[File:Wajinden_diagram.svg|thumb|map illustrating the path from the [[Daifang Commandery|Daifeng commandery]] to [[Yamatai]], and its distances in the [[Wajinden]]. See Matsurokoku around the middle for the locatiton of the shrine]]
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

{{Short description|Shinto Shrine on an Island in Saga Prefecture}} {{Draft topics|biography|literature|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}}
{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg | caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|33|21|N|129|53|26|E}} | location = Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}}|draft }} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-14 |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514023648/https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />. It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref> and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata [[File:Wajinden_diagram.svg|thumb|map illustrating the path from the [[Daifang Commandery|Daifeng commandery]] to [[Yamatai]], and its distances in the [[Wajinden]]. See Matsurokoku around the middle for the locatiton of the shrine]]
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg | caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|33|21|N|129|53|26|E}} | location = Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}}|draft }} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-14 |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514023648/https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />. It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref> and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata [[File:Wajinden_diagram.svg|thumb|map illustrating the path from the [[Daifang Commandery|Daifeng commandery]] to [[Yamatai]], and its distances in the [[Wajinden]]. See Matsurokoku around the middle for the locatiton of the shrine]]
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = 田島神社全景.jpg | caption = View of the shrine from the sea[[simple:Tashima Shrine]][[ja:田島神社]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|33|21|N|129|53|26|E}} | location = Japan | deity = * {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|draft}} * {{ill|Takiribime|ja|タキリビメ|draft}}|draft }} {{expand Japanese|田島神社|draft}}[[ja:田島神社]] {{afc comment|1=definitely notable[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 06:21, 3 November 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{ill|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple|6=draft|Tashima Shrine}} is a shrine situated on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}} in [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]] Town now, [[Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] City, [[Saga Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QNw5D3Br8BoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Japan Magazine: A Representative Monthly of Things Japanese |date=1928 |publisher=Japan magazine Company |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hall |first=Jessica |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bmiYUKjEBMoC&q=Tashima+Shrine |title=The Deepest Edge |date=2003 |publisher=Signet |isbn=978-0-451-20796-8 |language=en|draft}}</ref> It is located in the area known as [[Matsurokoku]], which is believed to be the first land of the mainland of [[Wakoku]] as per [[Wajinden]] records. It is an important point for safe sea crossings to the continent, and has received significant orders from the central government since ancient times.
In earlier times, it was called 'Tajima Niimasu Kaminoyashiro'. It is the only [[Myojin Taisha]] in [[Hizen Province]], and was previously classified as [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei Chusha]] due to renovations during the [[Meiji period]]. Currently, it is a [[beppyo shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-14 |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514023648/https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=web.archive.org}}</ref> It is associated with [[Matsura Sayohime]] who is said to be buried on the site<ref name="joya" /><ref name="japan-office1915" /><ref name="murao" />. It is a Munakata shrine<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kalland |first=Arne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wp4xhRXsARcC&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PA47 |title=Fishing Villages in Tokugawa, Japan |date=1995-01-01 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-1632-2 |language=en|draft}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rots |first1=Aike P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pcjZDwAAQBAJ&dq=Tashima+Shrine&pg=PT104 |title=Sacred Heritage in Japan |last2=Teeuwen |first2=Mark |date=2020-04-02 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-000-04563-5 |language=en|draft}}</ref> and is said to be the original shrine (roots) of [[Munakata Taisha]], so it is sometimes called Moto-Munakata [[File:Wajinden_diagram.svg|thumb|map illustrating the path from the [[Daifang Commandery|Daifeng commandery]] to [[Yamatai]], and its distances in the [[Wajinden]]. See Matsurokoku around the middle for the locatiton of the shrine]]
== Mythology == [[File:Princess Sayo at Matsu-ura.PNG|thumb|''Matsura Sayo-hime''. Caption refers to the petrification{{efn|"..{{nihongo|the vital force (''[[qi|ki]]'') of her love, in its exact original shape, transformed into stone|恋慕の気凝りて、そのままに形(かたち)石となり}}".}}{{Right|{{Small|—by [[Utagawa Kuniyoshi]]. Series: ''Kenjo reppuden'' or "Stories of Wise and Strong Women"<!--賢女烈婦伝-->.}}}}]]
According to a version of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]], she prayed with such fervour that she was transformed into stone.<ref name=pfoundes/> This petrification lore of Sayohime appears to be of later development, with its earliest attestation identified as [[renga]] poet {{illm|Bontōan|ja|梵灯庵|draft}}'s ''Sodeshita shū'' (c. [[Ōei]] era, late 14th to early 15th century).<ref name=nakayama-apud-yoshioka/> This lore of Sayohime's petrification is thought to have developed from a misunderstanding: a misreading of {{illm|Jikkinshō|ja|十訓抄|draft|lt=''Jikkinshō''}} (13th century), which ponders on the Sayohime legend and makes reference to the petrification motif taken from an old Chinese work called the {{illm|You Ming Lu|zh|幽明录|draft|lt=''Youminglu''}}.{{sfnp|Yabu|2006|p=19}}<ref name=ishikawa/> Sayohime's petrification is also mentioned in ''Nihon meijo monogatari'' (1670).<ref>{{harvp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=24–25}}; p. 21 (English abstract), ''apud'' {{harvp|Satō|1966|p=37}}</ref>
[[image:佐用姫神社 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Sayohime Shrine]] Her supposed petrified remains, an example of a {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}},{{sfnp|Kim Kyonran|1998|pp=21–22}} is housed as the ''[[shintai]]'' ("body of the kami") at the Sayohime Shrine, an [[Setsumatsusha|undershrine]] of {{illm|Tashima Shrine|ja|田島神社|simple}} on {{ill|Kabe Island|ja|加部島|ceb|Kabe_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Saga-ken)|draft}}.<ref name=joya/><ref name=japan-office1915/><ref name=murao/> The claim regarding her petrification on this island is given in a late account of the origin of this undershrine, preserved in the 19th century document called the {{nihongo|''Matsura komonjo''|松浦古文書}} (written during the [[Bunka]] era).<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> It states that the lady did not stop at the Scarf-Waving Peak bidding farewell, but she continued to a spot{{Refn|group="lower-alpha"|At the place she saw the island, she called out Satehiko's name, hence the spot was named {{nihongo|''Yobu na no ura''|呼名の浦|extra=lit. the 'name-calling inlet-shore'}}, which later became the town of [[Yobuko, Saga|Yobuko]].<ref name=matsura-komonjo/><ref name=matsushiro/><ref name=nipponica-matsurasayohime/>}} from whose vantage point she beheld an island nearby. She then hopped on a fishing boat to that island, called the {{nihongo|Himekami-jima|姫神島}} island (present-day Kabe Island<ref name=yoshida/><ref name=yanagita-meii/>) where she climbed a "bit elevated spot" and there, out of sorrow, she turned intorock.<ref name=matsura-komonjo/> Commentators identify this elevatation as the {{nihongo|Tendō-dake|天童岳}} or {{nihongo|Dentō-dake|伝登岳}}.<ref name=yoshida/>

{{複数の問題 | 出典の明記 = 2023年9月27日 (水) 17:41 (UTC) | 独自研究 = 2023年9月27日 (水) 17:41 (UTC) }} {{Otheruses|佐賀県唐津市の田島神社|佐賀県伊万里市の同名の神社|田嶋神社|大阪市生野区の同名の神社|田島神社 (大阪市)}} {{神社 |名称 = 田島神社 |画像 = [[File:田島神社全景.jpg|250px|全景]] |祭神 = [[タキリビメ|田心姫尊]]
[[イチキシマヒメ|市杵島姫尊]]
[[タギツヒメ|湍津姫尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（[[名神大社|名神大]]）
旧[[国幣中社]]
[[別表神社]] |所在地=佐賀県唐津市呼子町加部島3965 |緯度度=33|緯度分=33|緯度秒=21.0 |経度度=129|経度分=53|経度秒=26.0 |地図国コード = JP |地図=Japan Saga |ラベル位置=bottom }} '''田島神社'''（たしまじんじゃ）は、[[佐賀県]][[唐津市]][[呼子町]]（旧[[肥前国]][[松浦郡]]呼子）の[[加部島]]にある[[神社]]{{sfn|牧川|1902|p=113}}。地域は[[魏志倭人伝]]の中で倭国本土の最初の地として登場する[[末ら国|末盧国]]にあたる。大陸への最も安全な渡海ルートの要所であり、上代以来中央政府の重用を受けてきた。古代においては「田島坐神社（たじまにゐますかみのやしろ）」として記録されている。肥前国唯一の[[名神大社]]で、肥前国一之宮と見られた時代もあった。明治時代の改新による[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[国幣中社]]。現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。社紋は「桜紋」。[[山上憶良]]が歌に詠んだ[[松浦佐用姫]]ゆかりの神社。 ==祭神== 祭神は次の5柱。主祭神の3柱は[[宗像大社]]祭神の[[宗像三女神]]に同じ姫神。宇佐神宮や久留米周辺、天山、背振山にも祀られるなど、有史以前からの北部九州土着の神とされる。田島神社では「田島三神」と総称し、中でも田心姫尊を中尊としている。 ; 主祭神 :* [[タキリビメ|田心姫尊]] :* [[イチキシマヒメ|市杵島姫尊]] :* [[タギツヒメ|湍津姫尊]] ; 配祀神 :* [[オオヤマツミ|大山祇神]] :* 稚武王尊 - [[ヤマトタケル|日本武尊]]の子、[[仲哀天皇]]の弟。 ==歴史== === 創建 === 創建は不詳。一説には弥生時代後期とされている。『田島神の創祀と宗像神との関係について』　江永次男　昭和62年鎮座地の加部島はかつては「姫神の鎮座まします島」として「姫島」・「姫神島」と呼ばれていた。 [[天平]]3年（[[731年]]）に相殿に稚武王を配祀し、天平10年（[[738年]]）に[[聖武天皇]]より[[大伴古麻呂]]に詔命があり「田島大明神」の神号が贈られたとする。{{Cite book|和書|title=松浦古事記|publisher=|year=寛政元年と思われる}}　この天平3年を創始とする古書もある。 '''稚武王配祀と上松浦明神''' 稚武王（[[仲哀天皇]]の弟）の配祀については、[[神功皇后]]の[[三韓征伐]]より凱旋の折、「懇ろに奉斎されよ」と当社に駐留・警護を命じられたという逸話による。同じく[[平戸島|平戸]]に駐留を命じられたとする弟の十城別王を祀る[[志々伎神社]]は天平10年（738年）に「松浦明神」と崇められたとしている。{{Cite book|和書|title=肥前歴史叢書８　式内社　明神社　志々伎神社|date=1986.5.8|year=1986|publisher=芸文堂}}稚武王の「田島大明神」と十城別王の「松浦明神」は遣唐使廃止後の[[延喜式神名帳|延喜式神明帳]]（927年）の中では「上松浦明神」と「下松浦明神」となり、国防の要素の強い兄弟神社のような扱いになっている。 * [[延喜式]]巻第二十三　延喜式神明帳頭註　肥前松浦郡　「田嶋ハ仲哀帝ノ弟稚武王ナリ上松浦明神ト號スナリ。志々伎ハ稚武王ノ弟十城別王ナリ下松浦明神ト號スナリ。」 現在、田島神社より２㎞ほど離れた杉ノ原牧場（壱岐が目視でき、海原を見渡す広い視野が確保された場所）にある[[瓢塚古墳]]（佐賀県指定史跡）は内部が朱に塗られていたとのことから稚武王の墳墓とも言われている。{{Cite book|和書|title=西日本民俗文化考説|year=1988|publisher=九州大学出版会}} === 概史 === 『[[新抄格勅符抄]]』[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）牒によると、当時の「田島神（田嶋神）」には[[神戸 (民戸)|神戸]]として16戸が[[肥前国]]から充てられていた。 （「戸」とは戸籍作成上の最小集落単位のことで現代の感覚でいう1戸（軒）のことではなく「字」または「小字」にあたる。16戸ということは島内に限らず周辺地域一帯と見ることができる。この地域からの税収が神社の補修や催事の費用に充てられ、神官の俸給とすることは禁止されていた。） [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では肥前国[[松浦郡]]に「田島坐神社（田嶋坐神社） 名神大」と記載され、肥前国唯一の[[名神大社]]に列している。 [[江戸時代]]には[[唐津藩]]の[[祈願所]]となった。 [[明治維新]]後、1871年（[[明治]]4年）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列した。戦後は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に列している。 === 神階 === * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）1月27日、従五位下から従四位下 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * [[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]2年（[[860年]]）2月8日、従四位下から従四位上 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * 貞観15年（[[873年]]）9月16日、従四位上から正四位下 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * 貞観18年（[[876年]]）6月8日、従四位上{{sub|ママ}}から正四位下{{sub|ママ}} （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * [[元慶]]8年（[[884年]]）12月16日、正四位下から正四位上 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 国史の神階を受けた時代は実質的に最後の[[遣唐使]]となった第19回遣唐使帰還の後、まだ遣唐使廃止が決定されていない時期。久留米の[[高良大社]]、宗像の[[宗像大社]]の後を追いかけるように昇階していることから遣隋使・遣唐使運用上の連帯性が考えられる。 === 遣隋使・遣唐使 === 遣唐使の記録の中では、松浦の湊という漠然とした記載しか見うけられない。しかし、遣唐使直後の特別扱いとも言える昇階や朝廷の記録とリンクする社伝があることから単なる遣唐使の寄港地ではなく、朝廷に近い存在の宗像大社と協力し、北部九州沿岸土着の神社代表として積極的に関わっていたことが見て取れる。この地域は北ルート（呼子・壱岐・対馬ルート）に限らず、南ルート（五島より横断ルート）・南島ルートにおいても必ず通過する地点である。終始、土着の神社代表として遣隋使・遣唐使運航に積極的に関わり続けた結果が神階の特別扱いになったということが言える。{{Cite book|和書|title=古代諸国神社神階制の研究|date=2002年8月|year=2002年|publisher=岩田書院|pages=391－395頁}}六国史上、最後の昇階となる884年の43年後、延喜式神名帳（927）の中で肥前国佐賀県と壱岐・対馬を除く長崎県唯一の名神大社としての崇敬を受けているのも同じ理由と考えられる。 == 摂末社 == [[ファイル:20210207021831(8)b.jpg|サムネイル|343x343ピクセル|佐與姫神社]] *佐與姫神社（佐用姫神社）　佐用姫伝説の[[松浦佐用姫]]を祀る。佐用姫が変じたとされる石（望夫石）を御神体とし、覆う形で社殿が建てられている{{sfn|牧川|1902|p=116}}。田島神社境内の望夫石を見た豊臣秀吉が雨ざらしではあまりに忍びないと社領百石を佐用姫社に寄進したことで社殿が建てられたとし、寄進の朱印状が現存する。この社領は徳川政権の江戸時代も寄進され続けた。 * 御崎神社　御祭神は[[シナツヒコ|級長津彦神]]、[[級津姫神|級長津姫神]]、[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦神]]の三柱。[[文禄・慶長の役|文禄の役]]の際、軍船「小鷹丸」は大陸に七度の往復をし無事に帰国した。後年、その船体の一部が船霊の御守護と共に海上安全の守護神として祀られている。{{Cite book|和書|title=唐津名勝案内　牧川茂太郎編|date=1902.10.10|year=1902|publisher=此村書店|page=116}}　 この二社はどちらも地元特有の由緒を持つ神社である。境内には有名神社より勧請された分社や合祀社等は存在しない。しかし、島内には各地区に点在しており、田島神社の春祈祷の際に「区社参り」として祈祷に周る習わしがある。他に島内では各戸それぞれの庭の傍らに稲荷社を祀る家がとても多い。 == 祭事 == （太陽暦で記載） === [[歳旦祭]] === 1月1日　/　 === [[節分|節分祭]] === 2月3日　/　 === 春祈祷 === 4月1日～3日　/　通常の神事以外にも「区社参り」と称して島内の各地区で奉斎している小さな神社を各地区の代表皆でお参りして周る。木ノ宮、塚様、平嶽神社、天童神社（稲荷）、庚申様、[[瓢塚古墳|瓢塚]]、ヤブソ様、天神様が区社参りの対象である。 === 厄祓祈願祭 === 4月第2日曜日　/　　 === [[大祓|夏越祭]]・[[大祓]] === ７月最後の土曜日　/　夏越祭（夏越の大祓）は神社内での行事であるのが通例だが、現地の夏越祭は氏子が主催しお神輿で行列を組み民家近くの御旅所へ移動する。神様をお迎えして一晩膝を突き合わせて親しく過ごしつつ、夏越の祓を受けるという形になっている。（平成元年　平野良樹宮司談）　お神輿を担いでの移動なので、参道の第二鳥居にかけられる茅の輪の大きさも最大級となっている。以前は７月最後の土曜日・日曜日、さらにその前は29日・30日に行われていた。 '''歴史　'''現在の氏子主催の御旅所への神幸がどの時代から始まったものかは不明。昭和40年代前半の図書には神輿を船に乗せて呼子などの近隣に神幸する様子が写真入りで紹介されている。{{Cite book|和書|title=ふるさとの民俗　佐賀の芸能・祭り|year=1967|publisher=佐賀県文化館|page=136-137}}この時代には御旅所は現宝物館の場所に作られていた。古くは呼子側の小浜港、現小浜公園の東側、坂の上に御旅所があった時代もある。（石組みが現存） === 例祭 === 9月16日　/　 === [[新嘗祭]] === 11月23日　/　 === '''田島神社'''（たしまじんじゃ）は、[[佐賀県]][[唐津市]][[呼子町]]（旧[[肥前国]][[松浦郡]]呼子）の[[加部島]]にある[[神社]]{{sfn|牧川|1902|p=113}}。地域は[[魏志倭人伝]]の中で倭国本土の最初の地として登場する[[末ら国|末盧国]]にあたる。大陸への最も安全な渡海ルートの要所であり、上代以来中央政府の重用を受けてきた。古代においては「田島坐神社（たじまにゐますかみのやしろ）」として記録されている。肥前国唯一の[[名神大社]]で、肥前国一之宮と見られた時代もあった。明治時代の改新による[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[国幣中社]]。現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。社紋は「桜紋」。[[山上憶良]]が歌に詠んだ[[松浦佐用姫]]ゆかりの神社。 ==祭神== 祭神は次の5柱。主祭神の3柱は[[宗像大社]]祭神の[[宗像三女神]]に同じ姫神。宇佐神宮や久留米周辺、天山、背振山にも祀られるなど、有史以前からの北部九州土着の神とされる。田島神社では「田島三神」と総称し、中でも田心姫尊を中尊としている。 ; 主祭神 :* [[タキリビメ|田心姫尊]] :* [[イチキシマヒメ|市杵島姫尊]] :* [[タギツヒメ|湍津姫尊]] ; 配祀神 :* [[オオヤマツミ|大山祇神]] :* 稚武王尊 - [[ヤマトタケル|日本武尊]]の子、[[仲哀天皇]]の弟。 ==歴史== === 創建 === 創建は不詳。一説には弥生時代後期とされている。『田島神の創祀と宗像神との関係について』　江永次男　昭和62年鎮座地の加部島はかつては「姫神の鎮座まします島」として「姫島」・「姫神島」と呼ばれていた。 [[天平]]3年（[[731年]]）に相殿に稚武王を配祀し、天平10年（[[738年]]）に[[聖武天皇]]より[[大伴古麻呂]]に詔命があり「田島大明神」の神号が贈られたとする。{{Cite book|和書|title=松浦古事記|publisher=|year=寛政元年と思われる}}　この天平3年を創始とする古書もある。 '''稚武王配祀と上松浦明神''' 稚武王（[[仲哀天皇]]の弟）の配祀については、[[神功皇后]]の[[三韓征伐]]より凱旋の折、「懇ろに奉斎されよ」と当社に駐留・警護を命じられたという逸話による。同じく[[平戸島|平戸]]に駐留を命じられたとする弟の十城別王を祀る[[志々伎神社]]は天平10年（738年）に「松浦明神」と崇められたとしている。{{Cite book|和書|title=肥前歴史叢書８　式内社　明神社　志々伎神社|date=1986.5.8|year=1986|publisher=芸文堂}}稚武王の「田島大明神」と十城別王の「松浦明神」は遣唐使廃止後の[[延喜式神名帳|延喜式神明帳]]（927年）の中では「上松浦明神」と「下松浦明神」となり、国防の要素の強い兄弟神社のような扱いになっている。 * [[延喜式]]巻第二十三　延喜式神明帳頭註　肥前松浦郡　「田嶋ハ仲哀帝ノ弟稚武王ナリ上松浦明神ト號スナリ。志々伎ハ稚武王ノ弟十城別王ナリ下松浦明神ト號スナリ。」 現在、田島神社より２㎞ほど離れた杉ノ原牧場（壱岐が目視でき、海原を見渡す広い視野が確保された場所）にある[[瓢塚古墳]]（佐賀県指定史跡）は内部が朱に塗られていたとのことから稚武王の墳墓とも言われている。{{Cite book|和書|title=西日本民俗文化考説|year=1988|publisher=九州大学出版会}} === 概史 === 『[[新抄格勅符抄]]』[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）牒によると、当時の「田島神（田嶋神）」には[[神戸 (民戸)|神戸]]として16戸が[[肥前国]]から充てられていた。 （「戸」とは戸籍作成上の最小集落単位のことで現代の感覚でいう1戸（軒）のことではなく「字」または「小字」にあたる。16戸ということは島内に限らず周辺地域一帯と見ることができる。この地域からの税収が神社の補修や催事の費用に充てられ、神官の俸給とすることは禁止されていた。） [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では肥前国[[松浦郡]]に「田島坐神社（田嶋坐神社） 名神大」と記載され、肥前国唯一の[[名神大社]]に列している。 [[江戸時代]]には[[唐津藩]]の[[祈願所]]となった。 [[明治維新]]後、1871年（[[明治]]4年）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列した。戦後は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に列している。 === 神階 === * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）1月27日、従五位下から従四位下 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * [[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]2年（[[860年]]）2月8日、従四位下から従四位上 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * 貞観15年（[[873年]]）9月16日、従四位上から正四位下 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * 貞観18年（[[876年]]）6月8日、従四位上{{sub|ママ}}から正四位下{{sub|ママ}} （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * [[元慶]]8年（[[884年]]）12月16日、正四位下から正四位上 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 国史の神階を受けた時代は実質的に最後の[[遣唐使]]となった第19回遣唐使帰還の後、まだ遣唐使廃止が決定されていない時期。久留米の[[高良大社]]、宗像の[[宗像大社]]の後を追いかけるように昇階していることから遣隋使・遣唐使運用上の連帯性が考えられる。 === 遣隋使・遣唐使 === 遣唐使の記録の中では、松浦の湊という漠然とした記載しか見うけられない。しかし、遣唐使直後の特別扱いとも言える昇階や朝廷の記録とリンクする社伝があることから単なる遣唐使の寄港地ではなく、朝廷に近い存在の宗像大社と協力し、北部九州沿岸土着の神社代表として積極的に関わっていたことが見て取れる。この地域は北ルート（呼子・壱岐・対馬ルート）に限らず、南ルート（五島より横断ルート）・南島ルートにおいても必ず通過する地点である。終始、土着の神社代表として遣隋使・遣唐使運航に積極的に関わり続けた結果が神階の特別扱いになったということが言える。{{Cite book|和書|title=古代諸国神社神階制の研究|date=2002年8月|year=2002年|publisher=岩田書院|pages=391－395頁}}六国史上、最後の昇階となる884年の43年後、延喜式神名帳（927）の中で肥前国佐賀県と壱岐・対馬を除く長崎県唯一の名神大社としての崇敬を受けているのも同じ理由と考えられる。 == 摂末社 == [[ファイル:20210207021831(8)b.jpg|サムネイル|343x343ピクセル|佐與姫神社]] *佐與姫神社（佐用姫神社）　佐用姫伝説の[[松浦佐用姫]]を祀る。佐用姫が変じたとされる石（望夫石）を御神体とし、覆う形で社殿が建てられている{{sfn|牧川|1902|p=116}}。田島神社境内の望夫石を見た豊臣秀吉が雨ざらしではあまりに忍びないと社領百石を佐用姫社に寄進したことで社殿が建てられたとし、寄進の朱印状が現存する。この社領は徳川政権の江戸時代も寄進され続けた。 * 御崎神社　御祭神は[[シナツヒコ|級長津彦神]]、[[級津姫神|級長津姫神]]、[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦神]]の三柱。[[文禄・慶長の役|文禄の役]]の際、軍船「小鷹丸」は大陸に七度の往復をし無事に帰国した。後年、その船体の一部が船霊の御守護と共に海上安全の守護神として祀られている。{{Cite book|和書|title=唐津名勝案内　牧川茂太郎編|date=1902.10.10|year=1902|publisher=此村書店|page=116}}　 この二社はどちらも地元特有の由緒を持つ神社である。境内には有名神社より勧請された分社や合祀社等は存在しない。しかし、島内には各地区に点在しており、田島神社の春祈祷の際に「区社参り」として祈祷に周る習わしがある。他に島内では各戸それぞれの庭の傍らに稲荷社を祀る家がとても多い。 == 祭事 == （太陽暦で記載） === [[歳旦祭]] === 1月1日　/　 === [[節分|節分祭]] === 2月3日　/　 === 春祈祷 === 4月1日～3日　/　通常の神事以外にも「区社参り」と称して島内の各地区で奉斎している小さな神社を各地区の代表皆でお参りして周る。木ノ宮、塚様、平嶽神社、天童神社（稲荷）、庚申様、[[瓢塚古墳|瓢塚]]、ヤブソ様、天神様が区社参りの対象である。 === 厄祓祈願祭 === 4月第2日曜日　/　　 === [[大祓|夏越祭]]・[[大祓]] === ７月最後の土曜日　/　夏越祭（夏越の大祓）は神社内での行事であるのが通例だが、現地の夏越祭は氏子が主催しお神輿で行列を組み民家近くの御旅所へ移動する。神様をお迎えして一晩膝を突き合わせて親しく過ごしつつ、夏越の祓を受けるという形になっている。（平成元年　平野良樹宮司談）　お神輿を担いでの移動なので、参道の第二鳥居にかけられる茅の輪の大きさも最大級となっている。以前は７月最後の土曜日・日曜日、さらにその前は29日・30日に行われていた。 '''歴史　'''現在の氏子主催の御旅所への神幸がどの時代から始まったものかは不明。昭和40年代前半の図書には神輿を船に乗せて呼子などの近隣に神幸する様子が写真入りで紹介されている。{{Cite book|和書|title=ふるさとの民俗　佐賀の芸能・祭り|year=1967|publisher=佐賀県文化館|page=136-137}}この時代には御旅所は現宝物館の場所に作られていた。古くは呼子側の小浜港、現小浜公園の東側、坂の上に御旅所があった時代もある。（石組みが現存） === 例祭 === 9月16日　/　 === [[新嘗祭]] === 11月23日　/　 === '''田島神社'''（たしまじんじゃ）は、[[佐賀県]][[唐津市]][[呼子町]]（旧[[肥前国]][[松浦郡]]呼子）の[[加部島]]にある[[神社]]{{sfn|牧川|1902|p=113}}。地域は[[魏志倭人伝]]の中で倭国本土の最初の地として登場する[[末ら国|末盧国]]にあたる。大陸への最も安全な渡海ルートの要所であり、上代以来中央政府の重用を受けてきた。古代においては「田島坐神社（たじまにゐますかみのやしろ）」として記録されている。肥前国唯一の[[名神大社]]で、肥前国一之宮と見られた時代もあった。明治時代の改新による[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[国幣中社]]。現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。社紋は「桜紋」。[[山上憶良]]が歌に詠んだ[[松浦佐用姫]]ゆかりの神社。 ==祭神== 祭神は次の5柱。主祭神の3柱は[[宗像大社]]祭神の[[宗像三女神]]に同じ姫神。宇佐神宮や久留米周辺、天山、背振山にも祀られるなど、有史以前からの北部九州土着の神とされる。田島神社では「田島三神」と総称し、中でも田心姫尊を中尊としている。 ; 主祭神 :* [[タキリビメ|田心姫尊]] :* [[イチキシマヒメ|市杵島姫尊]] :* [[タギツヒメ|湍津姫尊]] ; 配祀神 :* [[オオヤマツミ|大山祇神]] :* 稚武王尊 - [[ヤマトタケル|日本武尊]]の子、[[仲哀天皇]]の弟。 ==歴史== === 創建 === 創建は不詳。一説には弥生時代後期とされている。『田島神の創祀と宗像神との関係について』　江永次男　昭和62年鎮座地の加部島はかつては「姫神の鎮座まします島」として「姫島」・「姫神島」と呼ばれていた。 [[天平]]3年（[[731年]]）に相殿に稚武王を配祀し、天平10年（[[738年]]）に[[聖武天皇]]より[[大伴古麻呂]]に詔命があり「田島大明神」の神号が贈られたとする。{{Cite book|和書|title=松浦古事記|publisher=|year=寛政元年と思われる}}　この天平3年を創始とする古書もある。 '''稚武王配祀と上松浦明神''' 稚武王（[[仲哀天皇]]の弟）の配祀については、[[神功皇后]]の[[三韓征伐]]より凱旋の折、「懇ろに奉斎されよ」と当社に駐留・警護を命じられたという逸話による。同じく[[平戸島|平戸]]に駐留を命じられたとする弟の十城別王を祀る[[志々伎神社]]は天平10年（738年）に「松浦明神」と崇められたとしている。{{Cite book|和書|title=肥前歴史叢書８　式内社　明神社　志々伎神社|date=1986.5.8|year=1986|publisher=芸文堂}}稚武王の「田島大明神」と十城別王の「松浦明神」は遣唐使廃止後の[[延喜式神名帳|延喜式神明帳]]（927年）の中では「上松浦明神」と「下松浦明神」となり、国防の要素の強い兄弟神社のような扱いになっている。 * [[延喜式]]巻第二十三　延喜式神明帳頭註　肥前松浦郡　「田嶋ハ仲哀帝ノ弟稚武王ナリ上松浦明神ト號スナリ。志々伎ハ稚武王ノ弟十城別王ナリ下松浦明神ト號スナリ。」 現在、田島神社より２㎞ほど離れた杉ノ原牧場（壱岐が目視でき、海原を見渡す広い視野が確保された場所）にある[[瓢塚古墳]]（佐賀県指定史跡）は内部が朱に塗られていたとのことから稚武王の墳墓とも言われている。{{Cite book|和書|title=西日本民俗文化考説|year=1988|publisher=九州大学出版会}} === 概史 === 『[[新抄格勅符抄]]』[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）牒によると、当時の「田島神（田嶋神）」には[[神戸 (民戸)|神戸]]として16戸が[[肥前国]]から充てられていた。 （「戸」とは戸籍作成上の最小集落単位のことで現代の感覚でいう1戸（軒）のことではなく「字」または「小字」にあたる。16戸ということは島内に限らず周辺地域一帯と見ることができる。この地域からの税収が神社の補修や催事の費用に充てられ、神官の俸給とすることは禁止されていた。） [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では肥前国[[松浦郡]]に「田島坐神社（田嶋坐神社） 名神大」と記載され、肥前国唯一の[[名神大社]]に列している。 [[江戸時代]]には[[唐津藩]]の[[祈願所]]となった。 [[明治維新]]後、1871年（[[明治]]4年）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列した。戦後は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に列している。 === 神階 === * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）1月27日、従五位下から従四位下 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * [[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]2年（[[860年]]）2月8日、従四位下から従四位上 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * 貞観15年（[[873年]]）9月16日、従四位上から正四位下 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * 貞観18年（[[876年]]）6月8日、従四位上{{sub|ママ}}から正四位下{{sub|ママ}} （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 * [[元慶]]8年（[[884年]]）12月16日、正四位下から正四位上 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「田島神（田嶋神）」。 国史の神階を受けた時代は実質的に最後の[[遣唐使]]となった第19回遣唐使帰還の後、まだ遣唐使廃止が決定されていない時期。久留米の[[高良大社]]、宗像の[[宗像大社]]の後を追いかけるように昇階していることから遣隋使・遣唐使運用上の連帯性が考えられる。 === 遣隋使・遣唐使 === 遣唐使の記録の中では、松浦の湊という漠然とした記載しか見うけられない。しかし、遣唐使直後の特別扱いとも言える昇階や朝廷の記録とリンクする社伝があることから単なる遣唐使の寄港地ではなく、朝廷に近い存在の宗像大社と協力し、北部九州沿岸土着の神社代表として積極的に関わっていたことが見て取れる。この地域は北ルート（呼子・壱岐・対馬ルート）に限らず、南ルート（五島より横断ルート）・南島ルートにおいても必ず通過する地点である。終始、土着の神社代表として遣隋使・遣唐使運航に積極的に関わり続けた結果が神階の特別扱いになったということが言える。{{Cite book|和書|title=古代諸国神社神階制の研究|date=2002年8月|year=2002年|publisher=岩田書院|pages=391－395頁}}六国史上、最後の昇階となる884年の43年後、延喜式神名帳（927）の中で肥前国佐賀県と壱岐・対馬を除く長崎県唯一の名神大社としての崇敬を受けているのも同じ理由と考えられる。 == 摂末社 == [[ファイル:20210207021831(8)b.jpg|サムネイル|343x343ピクセル|佐與姫神社]] *佐與姫神社（佐用姫神社）　佐用姫伝説の[[松浦佐用姫]]を祀る。佐用姫が変じたとされる石（望夫石）を御神体とし、覆う形で社殿が建てられている{{sfn|牧川|1902|p=116}}。田島神社境内の望夫石を見た豊臣秀吉が雨ざらしではあまりに忍びないと社領百石を佐用姫社に寄進したことで社殿が建てられたとし、寄進の朱印状が現存する。この社領は徳川政権の江戸時代も寄進され続けた。 * 御崎神社　御祭神は[[シナツヒコ|級長津彦神]]、[[級津姫神|級長津姫神]]、[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦神]]の三柱。[[文禄・慶長の役|文禄の役]]の際、軍船「小鷹丸」は大陸に七度の往復をし無事に帰国した。後年、その船体の一部が船霊の御守護と共に海上安全の守護神として祀られている。{{Cite book|和書|title=唐津名勝案内　牧川茂太郎編|date=1902.10.10|year=1902|publisher=此村書店|page=116}}　 この二社はどちらも地元特有の由緒を持つ神社である。境内には有名神社より勧請された分社や合祀社等は存在しない。しかし、島内には各地区に点在しており、田島神社の春祈祷の際に「区社参り」として祈祷に周る習わしがある。他に島内では各戸それぞれの庭の傍らに稲荷社を祀る家がとても多い。 == 祭事 == （太陽暦で記載） === [[歳旦祭]] === 1月1日　/　 === [[節分|節分祭]] === 2月3日　/　 === 春祈祷 === 4月1日～3日　/　通常の神事以外にも「区社参り」と称して島内の各地区で奉斎している小さな神社を各地区の代表皆でお参りして周る。木ノ宮、塚様、平嶽神社、天童神社（稲荷）、庚申様、[[瓢塚古墳|瓢塚]]、ヤブソ様、天神様が区社参りの対象である。 === 厄祓祈願祭 === 4月第2日曜日　/　　 === [[大祓|夏越祭]]・[[大祓]] === ７月最後の土曜日　/　夏越祭（夏越の大祓）は神社内での行事であるのが通例だが、現地の夏越祭は氏子が主催しお神輿で行列を組み民家近くの御旅所へ移動する。神様をお迎えして一晩膝を突き合わせて親しく過ごしつつ、夏越の祓を受けるという形になっている。（平成元年　平野良樹宮司談）　お神輿を担いでの移動なので、参道の第二鳥居にかけられる茅の輪の大きさも最大級となっている。以前は７月最後の土曜日・日曜日、さらにその前は29日・30日に行われていた。 '''歴史　'''現在の氏子主催の御旅所への神幸がどの時代から始まったものかは不明。昭和40年代前半の図書には神輿を船に乗せて呼子などの近隣に神幸する様子が写真入りで紹介されている。{{Cite book|和書|title=ふるさとの民俗　佐賀の芸能・祭り|year=1967|publisher=佐賀県文化館|page=136-137}}この時代には御旅所は現宝物館の場所に作られていた。古くは呼子側の小浜港、現小浜公園の東側、坂の上に御旅所があった時代もある。（石組みが現存） === 例祭 === 9月16日　/　 === [[新嘗祭]] === 11月23日　/　 ===
